facts.basis: Notes sound together, so the melody is taken as the top line: the highest note at each onset, among right-hand notes when there are any, leaving out notes under a melody note still held. Intervals are named by their size in semitones.

facts.basis: Counted from the tonic of A minor; ♯ and ♭ mark notes outside its natural minor scale. The key is stated by the file.

facts.text: Intervals by name: minor 2nd down, minor 2nd up, perfect 4th down, minor 3rd up, major 2nd down, minor 3rd down, major 6th down, major 3rd up, perfect 4th up, major 2nd up, perfect 5th down, major 3rd up and 5 more. Most common: a minor 2nd (4 of 17).
facts.basis: Notes sound together, so the melody is taken as the top line: the highest note at each onset, among right-hand notes when there are any, leaving out notes under a melody note still held. Names go by size in semitones, not by spelling.

facts.text: No note is repeated straight away.
facts.basis: Notes sound together, so the melody is taken as the top line: the highest note at each onset, among right-hand notes when there are any, leaving out notes under a melody note still held.

facts.text: 3 of 18 melody notes sound over lower notes: 3 struck together with them. 1 shares its pitch class with a lower note, so it is also part of the chord below: A4 (with A2).
facts.brief: 3 of 18 melody notes sound over lower notes.
facts.basis: The melody is the inferred top line. A lower note sounds with a melody note when it starts with it or is still held when it starts. A shared pitch class means the melody note is also a note of the chord under it.

facts.text: 1 phrase boundary inside the motif: at bar 4 beat 3, from a passage that comes back note for note.
facts.basis: Boundaries come from phrase slurs, rests of a beat or more and repeat signs in the source, from a passage that comes back note for note or starts again at once, and from boundaries the player set; where none of these marks one, none is invented. A boundary from a rest or a return alone is a reading of the notes, not a mark in the score.

facts.text: Lengths: 24 sixteenths, 3 eighths.
facts.basis: Read from the notes' lengths; a tied note counts as one length.

facts.text: Onsets fit the sixteenth-note grid. 12 of 24 onsets fall on a beat. It starts on beat 1 of bar 1.
facts.basis: Measured from the bar lines.

facts.text: No silence between notes.
facts.basis: Measured where no note of the motif sounds; rests in other voices or hands are not counted.

facts.text: Onsets per beat, bar by bar: 2 2 2 | 2 2 2 | 2 2 2 | 2 2 2. Every beat splits in two.
facts.basis: Counted per beat of the time signature, from the bar lines; notes that start together count as one onset.

facts.text: No syncopation: no onset off the beat is held into the next beat, and no note is held across the bar line from a weak beat.
facts.basis: An onset is syncopated when it starts off the beat and still sounds on the next beat, or starts on a beat other than the first and sounds across the bar line. Tied notes count as one note.

facts.text: No accents are marked on the motif's notes.
facts.basis: Read from the accent marks written in the file (> accent, ^ strong accent); loudness in the notes is not counted.

facts.text: Bars 1, 2, 3 and 4 have the same rhythm. The figure sixteenth–sixteenth fills 12 beats.
facts.brief: Bars 1, 2, 3 and 4 have the same rhythm.
facts.basis: Bars are compared by where their onsets fall from the bar line, counting only bars wholly inside the selection; figures by the onsets inside one beat. A beat holding one note on the beat is not a figure.

facts.text: Key: A minor.
facts.basis: The file states the key signature (no sharps or flats) and the mode.

facts.text: The motif recurs 5 times (5 exact, 0 transposed): exactly in bars 16–19, exactly in bars 40–43, exactly in bars 54–57, exactly in bars 84–87 and exactly in bars 98–101.
facts.brief: The motif recurs 5 times (5 exact, 0 transposed).
facts.basis: Notes sound together, so lines are taken as the highest note at each onset. A recurrence has the same onsets from its first note and every pitch moved by the same amount; note lengths are not compared.

facts.text: New material in bars 0–4, 7–15, 24–33, 36–37, 61–68, 74–79 and 82; the other 65 bars repeat an earlier bar, exactly or transposed.

character.text: Texture: a melody over broken chords in the left hand. The two parts take turns: the accompaniment sounds in the melody's pauses. The broken chords keep the harmony moving under the melody.
character.brief: A melody over broken chords in the left hand. The broken chords keep the harmony moving under the melody.
character.basis: Inferred from the hands: the right hand's notes are the melody, the left hand's the accompaniment, read as chords when half its onsets strike two notes or more, as broken chords when its single notes mostly leap, as taking turns when at most 4 in 10 of its onsets fall with the melody's, as long notes when they last a half note or more, otherwise as a bass line.
Read from the file's tempo map, in quarter notes per minute, rounded to a tenth for display.

character.text: Density: 2 onsets per beat (24 onsets over 12 beats); the busiest beat holds 2. Counting every note of a chord, 2.3 notes per beat.
character.basis: Counted over the beats of the selection, from the bar lines; notes that start together count as one onset.

character.text: Register: E2 to E5, a range of 36 semitones; 18 of 27 notes are at or above middle C, and the middle pitch is G♯4.
character.brief: Register: E2 to E5; 18 of 27 notes are at or above middle C.
character.basis: Measured over every note of the motif; middle C is C4. The middle pitch is the median, the lower of the two middle ones for an even count. Spelled for A minor.

character.text: Velocity: every note has 80, on the MIDI scale of 1 to 127.
character.basis: Read from the notes. A notation file holds no played loudness: velocities come from its dynamics marks, or the default of 80 where it has none.

character.text: Articulation: notes sound for 100% of the time to the next onset on average; 26 of 26 notes sound until the next onset, and 0 sound for less than half of it.
character.brief: Articulation: notes sound for 100% of the time to the next onset on average.
character.basis: Measured as each note's length over the time from its onset to the next onset of the motif, counting at most the whole gap; notes of the last onset have no next onset and are not counted. A notation file gives written lengths, and staccato or tenuto marks are not read, so this reflects the written note values rather than how they are played.

Onsets counted with the same rule as the syncopation fact. An onset is syncopated when it starts off the beat and still sounds on the next beat, or starts on a beat other than the first and sounds across the bar line. Tied notes count as one note.

facts.text: Harmonic motion: Am → E → Am, i → V → i (tonic → dominant → tonic). It comes to rest: the dominant pulls to the tonic and resolves into it, an authentic cadence.
facts.brief: Harmonic motion: i → V → i. It comes to rest: the dominant pulls to the tonic and resolves into it, an authentic cadence.
facts.basis: Inferred from the chords read from the notes, as steps of A minor: the first step is the tonic, the fourth and second the subdominant, the fifth and the leading note's chord the dominant; a chord with a note outside the key has no function. The last two chords name the cadence.

facts.text: 3 chords read from the notes: Am from bar 2, E from bar 3, Am from bar 4.
facts.basis: Inferred: the pitches sounding in each beat, weighed by how long they sound and with the lowest note counting most, are matched against major, minor, diminished, augmented, suspended and seventh chords; a beat whose notes fit the chord before it joins that chord.

facts.text: The bass plays 9 notes: A2 E3 A3 E2 E3 G♯3 A2 E3 A3. Its 8 moves are 8 leaps.
facts.basis: Inferred: the bass is the lowest note at each onset, among left-hand notes when there are any, leaving out notes over a bass note still held.

facts.text: The chord changes twice in 4 bars: about every 2 bars.
facts.basis: Inferred from the chords read from the notes: each change is where a new chord starts.

facts.text: From bass to top, the chords span from 2 octaves (Am, from bar 2) to 2 octaves and a perfect 5th (E, from bar 3); 3 of 3 are open, wider than an octave.
facts.brief: 3 of 3 chords are open, wider than an octave.
facts.basis: Measured from the lowest to the highest note sounding in each chord the finder read.

facts.text: Neighbouring chords share notes at 2 of 2 changes: Am–E: E; E–Am: E.
facts.brief: Neighbouring chords share notes at 2 of 2 changes.
facts.basis: Inferred from the chords read from the notes: a shared note is a pitch class in both chords.
